issues.title: Missing secret bypasses authentication
issues.reason: When `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset and the request omits the selected header, both expressions evaluate to `undefined`. The comparison therefore succeeds and an unauthenticated request reaches the credential decryption and database-write path. Enabling credential sharing without configuring the secret leaves this sensitive endpoint unprotected.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Fail closed unless `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is a non-empty string, then compare the request header against that configured value. Configuration validation at application startup would also prevent this deployment state.

issues.title: Concurrent requests create duplicate credentials
issues.reason: The read followed by a separate create is not atomic. Two first-time requests for the same user and app can both observe no credential and both execute `credential.create`. This leaves duplicate records, after which future calls update only whichever record `findFirst` happens to return. If uniqueness is enforced elsewhere, one otherwise valid concurrent request instead fails with an unhandled database error.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Enforce a unique `(userId, appId)` database constraint and use an atomic upsert against that key. If the data model intentionally permits multiple credentials, serialize this lookup/create operation and select the target deterministically.

issues.title: Fallback schema defines literal keys
issues.reason: Computed object keys are evaluated immediately, so these expressions create fixed string-named properties; they are not Zod index signatures. Consequently, ordinary OAuth responses can fail validation if the generated numeric property is required. If the two generated keys collide, the optional declaration replaces the numeric declaration, while Zod's default object behavior strips provider fields such as expiry metadata. This can break refreshes or discard token data whenever credential sharing is enabled.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Validate the required access token and preserve provider-specific properties with Zod's passthrough behavior. If numeric expiry validation is required, declare the known expiry fields explicitly in provider schemas rather than attempting a wildcard object property.

issues.title: Sync branch breaks caller response contracts
issues.reason:
When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native Fetch `Response` or abbreviated synchronization payload rather than the result shape expected from each provider callback. Google, Zoho CRM, and Zoho Bigin access Axios/Gaxios-style `.data`; HubSpot reads token fields directly; Lark expects its provider envelope; Webex validates provider metadata; and Office 365 Video derives expiry and replaces stored credentials using fields absent from the shared response. The mismatch causes exceptions, schema rejection, undefined access tokens, invalid expiry values, and loss of refresh tokens or provider metadata. Define and validate one token-result contract for both helper branches, reject unsuccessful synchronization responses, update callers to consume that contract, and preserve existing provider-specific credential fields when the shared result does not supply them.

Also affects: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:6, packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7, packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8, packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94, packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177, packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:67, packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:61, packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:62, packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:84, packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:204, packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:207
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Define one normalized token-result contract for this helper and adapt both branches to it, then update callers to consume that contract. Alternatively, accept a caller-provided adapter that converts the sync endpoint's `Response` into the same shape as that caller's `refreshFunction` result before returning it.

issues.title: Persists validation wrapper as credentials
issues.reason: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the complete Zod `safeParse` result, shaped like `{ success: true, data: credentials }`, rather than its `data`. This line therefore stores that wrapper in `credential.key`. The next service construction calls `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)`, which expects token fields at the top level and will reject the persisted value, breaking subsequent calendar operations after a successful refresh.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Persist the validated credential data rather than the safeParse wrapper. Change the helper to return `refreshTokenResponse.data` (and update its refresh-token fallback on that object), or unwrap `.data` at this call site.

issues.title: Refresh replaces valid token with placeholder
issues.reason: `refresh_token` is optional in `refreshTokenResponseSchema`, and Microsoft may omit it while returning a valid refreshed access token. The new parser inserts the literal `"refresh_token"` whenever it is absent. Line 264 then spreads that value over the existing credential, so the next access-token expiry attempts renewal using the placeholder and fails, requiring the user to reconnect.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Do not synthesize a refresh token. Leave the field absent so merging the parsed response preserves the credential's existing refresh token.

issues.title: Prisma is not imported
issues.reason: The complete post-change file contains no import or local declaration for `prisma`, yet the added refresh path calls it. Unlike the sibling Google calendar implementation, which explicitly imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:11), this file will fail TypeScript compilation with an unresolved identifier, preventing the Salesforce integration from building.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Import the existing Prisma client from `@calcom/prisma`.

issues.title: Shared refresh response lacks expires_in
issues.reason: When credential sharing is enabled, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` bypasses `zoomRefreshedTokenSchema` and accepts the shared endpoint's minimum response, which only guarantees an access token and a numeric expiry property. The adapter subsequently computes `key.expiry_date` exclusively from `newTokens.expires_in`. A shared response containing `expiry_date`, as permitted by that contract, therefore produces `NaN` and prevents a valid expiry from being persisted (or causes the database update to fail), breaking Zoom token refresh for shared credentials.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Define a stable shared response field such as `expiry_date`, then preserve that value when present and only derive an absolute expiry from `expires_in` for native Zoom responses. The shared-response schema should explicitly require the same standardized field.

issues.title: Zoho Bigin sends a credential ID as the synchronization user ID
issues.reason:
The Zoho Bigin refresh path passes `credentialId` to a helper whose third argument is explicitly a Cal.com `userId`. The helper serializes that value as `calcomUserId`, so the synchronization service receives an identifier from the wrong domain.
Evidence: PRF040 passes `credentialId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`, while PRF002 names that parameter `userId` and sends it as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`. Other integrations pass `credential.userId`.
Business impact: Expired Zoho Bigin credentials can fail to refresh; depending on synchronization-service lookup semantics, the request may also select credentials belonging to a different user.
Also affects: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Pass `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`, matching the helper contract and the other provider integrations.

observed_sources.binding: Observed source for issue_2, issue_4, issue_5, issue_7, packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8:

bound_source_assessment.reason: The proposed trigger requires an unset webhook secret while credential sharing remains enabled. Exact source defines APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED as a conjunction of the secret and encryption key; when CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, that expression is falsy and the handler's first branch returns 403 before the equality comparison or database-write path. Although two undefined values would compare as equal, that predicate is not reached under the claimed configuration.
